niche.diet: Thermally active vertebrates, canopy insects, mineral-rich nectar

body: Streamlined aerodynamic frame, massive compound eyes with fused corneal lenses, paired thermal pit organs, polarization-sensitive wing membranes

chains.trait: Massive, fused-cornea visual array spanning UV to thermal bands
links: Broadband resolution requires large aperture diameter
Diffraction limit scales linearly with wavelength
Thin atmosphere delivers unfiltered 210–5000 nm flux
Transparent spectral window & F-type stellar SED

skill.effect: The creature's broad-spectrum vision sweeps across its surroundings, revealing hidden prey, mineral deposits, and thermal vents. This brief clarity exposes concealed paths and vulnerabilities to nearby observers.

chains.weakness: Large corneal mass causes rapid aerodynamic drag and metabolic heat buildup during M-dwarf flares
observe: Corneal curvature shifts from blue to amber under flare
Thermal pits flare red when targeting warm-blooded prey
Wings tilt to align microvilli with sky polarization vectors

journal.en: It does not just watch the sky; it weighs every photon like a stone.

plausibility.summary: Retitle/limit Spectral Lock to photon bands ~210–1000 nm (UV, visible, NIR reflectance/emission where retinal opsins or similar still apply); keep ~10 μm prey/vent mapping on pit organs only (Heat Trace). Optional highly speculative: separate dorsal 'NIR-bright' facets for 900 nm bias (F2), not LWIR in the eye.
fixes: Retitle/limit Spectral Lock to photon bands ~210–1000 nm (UV, visible, NIR reflectance/emission where retinal opsins or similar still apply); keep ~10 μm prey/vent mapping on pit organs only (Heat Trace). analogues.organism: Stomatopod compound eyes with regionalized spectral/polarization channels (not LWIR); pit viper/boa eyes for short-wave vision plus separate pit organs for IR—never one retinal stack spanning UV to 10 μm.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Dorsal polarization-sensitive ommatidia for celestial compass use
links: Rayleigh scattering creates predictable zenith polarization patterns
Low aerosol loading preserves high contrast polarization vectors
Sparse cloud cover & thin atmosphere maintain stable sky maps

skill.effect: The creature reads polarized light patterns to steer its flight, gliding smoothly through narrow rift valleys without losing its way. It completely ignores magnetic interference while navigating.

chains.weakness: Overcast or ash-choked skies scramble polarization maps, causing disorientation
observe: Dorsal eye facets rotate independently to track zenith
Flight paths straighten when aligned with polarized skylight
Landing posture mimics wind direction via microvilli alignment

journal.en: It reads the sky like braille, tracing invisible lines that never bend.

plausibility.summary: Rayleigh sky polarization with high zenith contrast (F11) and low aerosol load (F9) matches known animal navigation: dorsal rim or specialized ommatidia track polarization e-vector patterns for compass bearing, independent of weak planetary magnetism (F7). Sparse cloud and rift-corridor flight make polarization more reliable than magnetic cues. Overcast/ash disruption is a realistic weakness.
fixes: Rayleigh sky polarization with high zenith contrast (F11) and low aerosol load (F9) matches known animal navigation: dorsal rim or specialized ommatidia track polarization e-vector patterns for compass bearing, independent of weak planetary magnetism (F7). Sparse cloud and rift-corridor flight make polarization more reliable than magnetic cues. Overcast/ash disruption is a realistic weakness.

analogues.organism: Honeybee and desert ant dorsal polarization vision for skylight compass; monarch and dung beetle polarization navigation.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Paired infrared pit organs flanking the snout for heat mapping
links: Long-wave IR requires thermal differential detection, not photon capture
900 nm NIR bias lacks thermal contrast for retinal imaging
TRPA1 channels detect ambient heat maps via membrane deformation
Binary star NIR output & atmospheric transparency

skill.effect: The creature's infrared pits detect nearby warmth, pinpointing living targets and geothermal vents. This allows it to launch sudden ambushes or locate secure resting spots.

chains.weakness: Pit organs suffer thermal noise from direct sunlight; must use shadows or burrow to reset baseline
observe: Snout tilts downward to scan ground heat signatures
Pit membranes flush blue when cooled, red when warmed
Hunts only when self-cast shadows cover prey

journal.en: It feels the world’s breath before it sees the creature breathing it.

plausibility.summary: Split ranges: ~2–4 m for thermally active vertebrates/insects in shadow; up to ~15 m for large vents/warm rock faces. Mark volant pit-predator as highly speculative—justify via secondarily aerial lineage from pit-equipped cliff gliders/hunters on F12 rifts, not primary bird analogue.

chains.trait: Dermal melanin-analogues and rapid photolyase enzyme cycling
links: High UV-B/C flux causes rapid thymine dimering in DNA
Cross-linked polymers scatter UV while dissipating heat as IR
Enzymatic repair consumes metabolic budget proportional to flare frequency

skill.effect: The creature activates specialized skin polymers that scatter intense sunlight, greatly reducing the impact of solar flares. While this protection holds, its movements become noticeably slower.

chains.weakness: Prolonged flare activity depletes photolyase reserves, leaving tissues vulnerable to mutation and fatigue
observe: Skin shifts from iridescent blue to matte gray under flares
Eyes squint partially via nictitating UV filters
Resting posture minimizes surface area to direct sun

journal.en: It wears the sun’s violence like armor, paying for it in blood.

plausibility.summary: If lineage is framed as mammal-like aerial vertebrate, note placental mammals largely lack photolyase (rely on NER)—either invoke avian/reptilian biochemistry for Ojolarca or add 'photolyase-retaining' highly speculative deep ancestry.
fixes: If lineage is framed as mammal-like aerial vertebrate, note placental mammals largely lack photolyase (rely on NER)—either invoke avian/reptilian biochemistry for Ojolarca or add 'photolyase-retaining' highly speculative deep ancestry.

analogues.organism: Cyanobacteria and plants with photolyase + UV-screening pigments; reptiles and birds with epidermal melanin and behavioural shade-seeking under high UV.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

secrets: The fused cornea can temporarily split into three independent apertures, allowing it to track two targets and one polarized signal simultaneously, but causes severe metabolic exhaustion.
Pit organs can be temporarily blinded by coincident UV flares, forcing the creature to rely on low-frequency vocal sacs for 30 seconds while sensors reset.
moments: At dawn, the rift wind carries it upward on a thermal column. Its eyes lock onto a single polarized star, and for a breath it hangs perfectly still, a living instrument tuning itself to the sky before diving into the glare.

journal.en: It trades sharpness for survival, squinting at a world that never blinks.
It reads the water’s skin like a courtship letter, written in invisible ink.
